newsitem.title: UK: Reuters to return cash via special dividends.
newsitem.headline: Reuters to return cash via special dividends.

text.p: Reuters Holdings Plc said on Wednesday it proposed to return 613 million pounds ($953.3 million) of cash to shareholders over three years through a bonus issue of a new class of special dividend shares.
Under the proposal and a share capital consolidation, shareholders will receive 19 ordinary shares and one special dividend share for every 20 shares held on October 8.

Each special dividend share will pay net dividends totalling 750 pence over the period against an average of the ordinary share price of 752 pence for the week to 9 September 1996, the international news and information organisation said.

Reuters had already said it was looking at ways of returning surplus cash to shareholders. However, in the statement it said, "It was not possible to repeat the share repurchase structure which was adopted in 1993." It said UK tax clearance was not available for such a structure this time.
Reuters shares rose on news of the cash distribution. The shares rose 29 pence to 779 after reversing a five pence decline it showed immediately prior to the news.
Reuters said in a statement the share capital consolidation allows easy comparison with past performance of both earnings per share (EPS) and the ordinary share price.
The proposal is not expected to have any significant impact on EPS. The consolidation results in a five percent reduction in the number of ordinary shares in issue, the company said.

Under the scheme, holders of American Depositary Receipts (ADRs), will receive one special dividend American Depositary Share (ADS) and 19 new ADSs for every 20 ADSs held at the close of business on 8 October 1996.
Reuters said the payment will not diminish its high levels of investment for future growth.
"The company considers the proposal to be the best way of enabling shareholders to receive more cash, more efficiently, at a faster rate and on an equal basis," it said.
Reuters said comprehensive UK tax clearance had not been granted for the present proposal.
"However, based on advice, the company believes this proposal avoids any tax disadvantage for existing shareholders in respect of their current holdings," it said.
It said an on-market share repurchase was effectively ruled out because of the high proportion of holders in the U.S. and the Board's objective of treating all shareholders equally.
Each special dividend share will pay six net dividends over the next three years of 125p each, giving total special dividends per share of 750p, the company said.
SBC Warburg is independently offering to shareholders outside the U.S., Canada, Australia and Japan a special share dealing facility in Britain for the Special Dividend Shares, the company added.
The proposal will be voted on at an extraordinary general meeting of the company set for October 9.
Reuters has applied for the special dividend shares to be listed in the Britain and the ADSs in the U.S. Trading in these shares is expected to begin on October 10.
The company said the proposal will result in the company having returned nearly one billion pouns of surplus cash to shareholders in the 1990s, in addition to ordinary dividends. ($1=.6430 Pound)
